# Amplification QC

This report shows amplification curves grouped by biological sample
and target strain.

Colored curves are the technical replicate wells for the indicated
sample and strain. Grey curves show other wells from the same
plate/fluorophore combination for comparison.

```{r}
#| label: amplification-plots
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Determine which day x sample x strain combinations to plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

samples_to_plot <- qpcr_full %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(sample_type),
    sample_type == "sediment slurry",
    !is.na(sample),
    !is.na(strain),
    !is.na(day)
  ) %>%
  distinct(
    day,
    sample,
    strain,
    sediment,
    treatment,
    replicate
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    day_num = as.numeric(day)
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    day_num,
    sediment,
    treatment,
    replicate,
    sample,
    strain
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Loop through:
#
# Day
#   -> Sample
#       -> Strain
#           -> amplification plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

days_to_plot <- samples_to_plot %>%
  distinct(day, day_num) %>%
  arrange(day_num)


for (d_i in seq_len(nrow(days_to_plot))) {

  day_current <- days_to_plot$day[d_i]

  # ==========================================================
  # DAY HEADING
  # ==========================================================

  cat(
    "\n\n# Day ",
    day_current,
    "\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  # Samples occurring on this day
  day_samples <- samples_to_plot %>%
    filter(day == day_current) %>%
    distinct(
      sample,
      sediment,
      treatment,
      replicate
    ) %>%
    arrange(
      sediment,
      treatment,
      replicate,
      sample
    )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Loop through samples within this day
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  for (sample_i in seq_len(nrow(day_samples))) {

    sample_current <- day_samples$sample[sample_i]
    sediment_current <- day_samples$sediment[sample_i]
    treatment_current <- day_samples$treatment[sample_i]
    replicate_current <- day_samples$replicate[sample_i]


    # ========================================================
    # SAMPLE HEADING
    # ========================================================

    cat(
      "\n\n## Sample ",
      sample_current,
      "\n\n",
      sep = ""
    )


    # Sample metadata
    cat(
      "**Sediment:** ", sediment_current,
      "  \n",
      "**Treatment:** ", treatment_current,
      "  \n",
      "**Biological replicate:** ", replicate_current,
      "\n\n",
      sep = ""
    )


    # Find strains measured for this sample on this day
    strains_current <- samples_to_plot %>%
      filter(
        day == day_current,
        sample == sample_current
      ) %>%
      distinct(strain) %>%
      arrange(strain) %>%
      pull(strain)


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Loop through strains
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    for (strain_current in strains_current) {


      # ======================================================
      # STRAIN HEADING
      # ======================================================

      cat(
        "\n\n### ",
        strain_current,
        "\n\n",
        sep = ""
      )


      # Generate amplification plot
      p <- plot_amp_sample_strain(
        sample_check = sample_current,
        strain_check = strain_current,
        day_check = day_current,
        amplification = amplification,
        qpcr_full = qpcr_full
      )


      # Print plot
      if (!is.null(p)) {

        print(p)

      } else {

        cat(
          "\n*No amplification data available for this ",
          "sample × strain × day combination.*\n\n",
          sep = ""
        )
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
